sense: something to aim or shoot at

terms.gloss: a target, a mark to aim at
terms.comment: Greek σκοπός. Lewis & Short find it in Suetonius (Dom. 19), but the edition used here reads prō scopulō there, and Cicero writes the word in Greek letters (Att. 8.11.2).

phrases.latin: nōnnumquam in puerī procul stantis praebentisque prō scopulō dispānsam dexterae manūs palmam sagittās tantā arte dērēxit, ut omnēs per intervālla digitōrum innocuē ēvāderent
phrases.english: sometimes a boy stood far off and held up the open palm of his right hand as a target, and he shot his arrows at it so skilfully that they all passed harmlessly between the fingers

sources: Lewis & Short: scopus · Lewis & Short: scopulus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 45.
Suetonius, Domitian (Ihm), checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
